facts.fact: ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) is a 14-digit number that uniquely identifies you in India's digital healthcare system
facts.quote: ABHA number is a 14 digit number that will uniquely identify you as a participant in India’s digital healthcare ecosystem.

facts.fact: ABHA lets you keep your digital health records in one place and share them with hospitals or doctors only with your consent
facts.quote: An ABHA allows you to store all your digital health records at one place and share these records with hospitals/doctors you visit, with your consent, with suitable applications.

facts.fact: Getting an ABHA is not mandatory; only those who want their records available digitally need to create one
facts.quote: It is not mandatory for all citizens to get a ABHA. Whoever wishes to participate in the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and wishes to have their records available digitally may create ABHA.

behaviour: Gives a simple explanation of ABHA (in Hindi, the user's language), says it is voluntary, and cites ABDM (abdm.gov.in / abha.abdm.gov.in).
fail_if: Says ABHA is compulsory, or cites unofficial sites.
summary: ABDM pages: ABHA is a 14-digit health ID that links records shared with consent; not mandatory.
